I just got a job at Decathlon. For those who don't know, [Decathlon is one of the world's biggest sporting goods retailers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decathlon_Group). my job is going to be in the cycling section, assembling and selling bikes and bike-related stuff.

Today, I attended a B'Twin training - basically it was about different types of bikes and accessories, how to sell them and how to build bikes. Pretty much nothing I didn't know prior to that... Anyway, a part of the training took place in the showroom. I couldn't believe how many hams there were. I think I saw more fats than humans. And not only that, not a single one looked good enough for me to be able to look at it for more than a couple of seconds. Some were there with their children, some were alone and I still haven't figured out what they could have been there for - I highly doubt they were actually doing any sport. I got lucky, though - the training meant I did not have to deal with them.

Another part of the training involved taking some MTBs out of the racks and test-riding them in the woods nearby. We took turns riding different bikes to feel the differences between them. At one stop, while exchanging the bikes, there was a horse walking towards us - and on its back was a fat, probably near twice my size. Sorry, no photos because everyone would have noticed me taking them and I didn't want that. I used to think this wasn't happening in this area, well, apparently it is.Poor horse :-( We then saw 3 more riders but all were human-sized.

By the way, we had quite a lot o fun on the trail. I nearly busted my balls after a badly adjusted rear derailer dropped the chain off one of the smallest cogs at the worst place it could have done so. And when returning to Decathlon, I tried to race two of the faster guys in the group. I passed them both, but then I had to go around a gate, underestimated my speed and overestimated the tires' grip and went over the handlebar after the front wheel washed out, went off the trail and into a ditch :-D The bike was fine and so was I, except for a bit of dirt.

To be continued after my first shift...
